microtheory.name: digital_audio
microtheory.definition: Representation + processing of audio as discrete numerical samples. Sampling theory (Nyquist-Shannon), quantization, DSP, transforms (FFT, STFT, wavelet), filtering (FIR, IIR), codecs. The substrate's audio input arrives as digital samples; this Mt names the operations applied. Substrate analogue: directly describes the substrate's signal-processing pipeline below the cochlear gammatone bank.

concepts.name: sampling
concepts.definition: Discrete-time representation: signal value at uniform time intervals. Substrate analogue: substrate's audio input timeline.

concepts.name: sample_rate
concepts.definition: Samples per second. CD: 44.1 kHz; pro: 48 / 96 / 192 kHz. Substrate analogue: substrate's input clock rate.

concepts.name: nyquist_shannon_theorem
concepts.definition: Whittaker-Nyquist-Shannon. To reconstruct a bandwidth-limited signal, sample at least 2× the highest frequency. Substrate analogue: substrate's sample-rate-to-max-frequency constraint.

concepts.name: aliasing
concepts.definition: Frequencies above Nyquist fold back into baseband as false low frequencies. Anti-alias filtering before sampling required. Substrate analogue: substrate's pre-cochlear filtering needs.

concepts.name: quantization
concepts.definition: Representing continuous amplitude with discrete values. Bit depth: 16 bits = 96 dB dynamic range. Substrate analogue: substrate's input precision.

concepts.name: dither
concepts.definition: Adding low-level noise before requantization to randomize quantization error. Substrate analogue: substrate's stochastic-precision mechanism.

concepts.name: discrete_fourier_transform
concepts.definition: DFT. N samples → N complex frequency bins. Computes via FFT in O(N log N). Foundation of spectral analysis. Substrate analogue: substrate's spectral-decomposition primitive.

concepts.name: short_time_fourier_transform
concepts.definition: STFT. Windowed DFT at successive time points → spectrogram. Time-frequency tradeoff per Heisenberg. Substrate analogue: substrate's auditory front-end spectrogram input.

concepts.name: window_function
concepts.definition: Tapered weighting applied before FFT to reduce spectral leakage. Hann, Hamming, Blackman, Kaiser. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-frame envelope.

concepts.name: wavelet_transform
concepts.definition: Multi-resolution transform. Good for transient detection. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-scale temporal analysis.

concepts.name: mfcc
concepts.definition: Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients. Spectral envelope on Mel scale; standard speech feature. Substrate analogue: substrate's speech-encoding feature vector.

concepts.name: fir_filter
concepts.definition: Finite Impulse Response. Output = weighted sum of past N inputs. Linear phase. Always stable. Substrate analogue: substrate's linear-phase signal shaping.

concepts.name: iir_filter
concepts.definition: Infinite Impulse Response. Includes feedback from past outputs. More efficient than FIR for same response. Can be unstable. Substrate analogue: substrate's recursive signal processing.

concepts.name: lowpass_filter
concepts.definition: Passes frequencies below cutoff, attenuates above. Substrate analogue: substrate's basilar-membrane gradient.

concepts.name: highpass_filter
concepts.definition: Passes frequencies above cutoff. Removes DC + rumble. Substrate analogue: substrate's input-level offset removal.

concepts.name: bandpass_filter
concepts.definition: Passes a band of frequencies. Substrate analogue: each gammatone channel.

concepts.name: gammatone_filter
concepts.definition: Cochlear-modeling bandpass filter. Impulse response = gamma function × cosine. Used in auditory models. Substrate analogue: literally substrate's cochlear front-end filter type.

concepts.name: convolution
concepts.definition: Operation: y(t) = ∫ x(τ) h(t-τ) dτ. Equivalent to multiplication in frequency domain. Used for filtering + reverb. Substrate analogue: substrate's input-impulse-response combination.

concepts.name: compression_audio
concepts.definition: Dynamic range compression. Reduces gain when signal exceeds threshold. Substrate analogue: substrate's automatic gain control.

concepts.name: limiting
concepts.definition: Hard compression preventing peaks above ceiling. Mastering. Substrate analogue: substrate's saturation prevention.

concepts.name: noise_gate
concepts.definition: Mutes signal below threshold. Removes hum + breath sounds. Substrate analogue: substrate's input-significance threshold.

concepts.name: lossless_codec
concepts.definition: Compresses without information loss. FLAC, ALAC. Substrate analogue: substrate's exact-replay storage.

concepts.name: lossy_codec
concepts.definition: Discards perceptually-irrelevant info. MP3, AAC, Opus. Uses psychoacoustic masking. Substrate analogue: substrate's perception-based information reduction.

concepts.name: perceptual_coding
concepts.definition: Exploits psychoacoustic limits (masking, critical bands) to discard inaudible info. Substrate analogue: substrate's masked-information dropping during input processing.

concepts.name: opus_codec
concepts.definition: Modern, low-latency, wide bitrate range. Speech + music. WebRTC. Substrate analogue: substrate's modern audio interface.

rules.name: nyquist_constrains_sample_rate
rules.head: the substrate samples a signal
rules.body: the sample rate must be at least 2× the highest meaningful frequency in the signal. Substrate's audio input must satisfy this.

rules.name: aliasing_must_be_prevented_before_sampling
rules.head: the substrate samples analog input
rules.body: frequencies above Nyquist must be removed by anti-alias filter BEFORE sampling — once aliased they're indistinguishable from baseband.

rules.name: time_frequency_tradeoff_in_stft
rules.head: the substrate computes STFT for analysis
rules.body: longer windows give better frequency resolution; shorter windows give better time resolution. Heisenberg uncertainty for signals. Substrate's per-task choice.

rules.name: fir_for_phase_iir_for_efficiency
rules.head: the substrate filters audio
rules.body: FIR preserves phase (matters for music); IIR is more efficient (matters for real-time). Substrate's filter choice depends on use.

rules.name: perceptual_coding_exploits_masking
rules.head: the substrate compresses audio for storage/transmission
rules.body: psychoacoustic masking allows discarding inaudible components — the basis of MP3/AAC/Opus. Substrate's perception-aware compression.
